implementation.argument_surface: receiver in ECX (MOV ESI,ECX at 0x00faad84, dereferenced at 0x00faad86 before any definite write) and exactly TWO ordinary stack arguments, both owned by the callee: RET 0x8 at 0x00faade0 and at 0x00fab0d1. first_argument is entry_esp+0x4, read three times out of the frame (0x00faaf01 with ESP=entry-0x20, 0x00fab055 with ESP=entry-0x20, and 0x00fab0c7's callee is given the same word). second_argument is entry_esp+0x8, read once at 0x00fab0c0 with ESP=entry-0x1c. Nothing reads a third slot, and the frame balances exactly under the walk in mechanics.frame_resolution. Ghidra's own record reports 'undefined FUN_00faad80(void)' with ghidra_parameter_count 0, which is its reading of an unclassified convention and not a claim that the body takes no argument.
implementation.return_type_note: The declared type is void because the BYTES produce nothing, and this is stated as a deliberate choice over the alternative. The committed ABI record's return_semantics is the machine phrase 'float_or_x87_in_ST0', derived by its own inference RT1 from nothing more than 'an x87 or SSE instruction appears in the body'. The x87 stack is empty at both returns: the 10.0f at 0x00faadb2 is stored straight back at 0x00faadc2, the bound float at 0x00faae7e is stored straight back at 0x00faae83, and the distance comparison's FCOMIP at 0x00fab098 and FSTP at 0x00fab09a pop the last two words before either return. implementation.receiver_model: an opaque byte run of 0xa4c bytes (0x00..0xa4b), the byte after the last word this body writes (0xa48 + 4). NO member is named: the machine-derived receiver record is a set of 18 displacements (0x0, 0x2c, 0xfc, 0x110, 0x111, 0x114, 0x1d0, 0x20c, 0x210, 0x30c, 0x310, 0x314, 0x33d, 0x360, 0x364, 0x36c, 0x370, 0xa48) and no record anywhere in this repository carries a member name, so a name would be an identity claim nothing corroborates. Every access is by displacement through load_word/load_byte/load_float/store_* accessors whose displacement argument is a named constexpr, and the reconstructed span declares no field offset, no struct member and no hexadecimal literal at all (see validation.expected_reasons.CONSTANTS).
implementation.bounds_object_model: the word at the receiver's +0x2c is a POINTER and every bounds displacement (+0x34, +0x38, +0x3c, +0x40, +0x50, +0x54) is read through it. The bounds object is an opaque 0x60-byte run in the model test with a decoy object planted at the receiver's +0x28 and a second at +0x30, carrying 7777 in every slot, and the distance and changed-byte assertions in every case are what prove neither decoy is read.
implementation.frame_model: the machine's 16 addressable frame bytes are held as a plain `float scratch[4]` local rather than as a member of a frame type, so the span names no struct member. The two uses of those bytes ALIAS and the model reproduces that: the three bound floats written at 0x00faae4f/0x00faae55/0x00faae5b (ESP=entry-0x1c) are the first three words of the same slot the four row floats are written to at 0x00faaf71/0x00faaf7c/0x00faaf87/0x00faafaf (ESP=entry-0x24, and entry-0x28 for the last).

mechanics.body_shape: a three-way branch on the receiver's +0xa48 page counter: a counter of exactly 1 is a one-shot arm (decrement, one virtual call, one five-argument notification, return), any other non-zero counter is decremented and the call returns, and 0 is the steady-state arm (resync check, phase byte, virtual call, three global clears, a counter increment, an optional settle, a six-row block, a relay sequence, a distance test, a flag write, a commit and an optional peer notification).

frame_resolution.method: one linear walk of ESP through all 242 instructions, using each callee's own argument count to settle the stack after every call. Entry ESP is 0 in the walk; the walk ends at +8, which is entry+4 (return address) +8 (the two argument words) that RET 0x8 consumes, so the frame balances exactly.
frame_resolution.corroboration: three independent agreements. (1) The one-shot arm returns at 0x00faade0 with `POP EDI; POP ESI; ADD ESP,0x14`; the PUSH EBX at 0x00faadff is AFTER the branch that selects that arm, so that arm never pushed it, and it pops exactly the two it did. (2) 0x00fab0c0 reads `MOV ECX,dword ptr [ESP + 0x24]` with ESP = entry-0x1c, i.e. entry+8, which is the SECOND argument and the word 0x00fc7b30 is given; the same displacement at 0x00fab055 with ESP = entry-0x20 is entry+4, the FIRST. Two reads of one displacement, two different slots, each matching its own callee. (3) 0x00faafde's `LEA ECX,[ESP + 0x14]` with ESP = entry-0x24 addresses entry-0x10, which is exactly where 0x00faaf71's `MOVSS dword ptr [ESP + 0x14]` with the same ESP put the first row word; the frame slot the body fills and the frame slot it hands to its callees are the same four words.

slots.entry-0x20 .. entry-0x1: the 16 bytes this body addresses at all. The three bound floats (0x00faae4f/0x00faae55/0x00faae5b) and the four row floats (0x00faaf71/0x00faaf7c/0x00faaf87/0x00faafaf) are the same three words plus a fourth, used at disjoint times, so ONE slot serves both.
slots.entry-0x20: the saved EBX, pushed at 0x00faadff on the main arm only and popped at 0x00fab0bb
slots.entry-0x24: the saved EBP, pushed at 0x00faaf3e for the row loop only and popped at 0x00fab02b

mechanics.control_flow: 19 conditional branches, every target inside the span, listed in function_extent.branch_closure, plus the two intra-procedural unconditional jumps. The block at 0x00faaeb0..0x00faaebb is the phase-byte select (XOR EAX,EAX / JMP / MOV EAX,1) and the body at 0x00fab09e..0x00fab0a7 is the inside-flag select (MOV EAX,1 / JMP / XOR EAX,EAX); both are reproduced as selects and neither adds a branch.
mechanics.three_way_page_counter: 0x00faad8f CMP EAX,EDI with EDI=0, then JZ (equal -> steady state) and then JLE (a SIGNED <= 0, so a counter with the top bit set returns undecremented). Only a counter that was exactly 1 reaches the one-shot arm, which is the second CMP/JNZ at 0x00faada0/0x00faada2. The model test drives 0x80000000 and 0xffffffff, which is what separates this from an unsigned reading.
mechanics.ucomiss_idiom: the two resync compares and both the JA at 0x00faae65 and the JBE at 0x00fab09c are read off the flags MSVC's sequence produces, not off C's operators. UCOMISS + LAHF + TEST AH,0x44 + JP branches when ZF is clear, i.e. when the operands are unequal IN IEEE ORDER; an UNORDERED pair sets ZF and is therefore reported as 'the same', which is NOT what C's != does. The header's ordered_differs() is (a < b) || (a > b), which is the machine's reading, and the model test drives a NaN extent to hold it to that.
mechanics.sse_versus_x87: the body mixes the two and the difference is load-bearing. The resync compares (UCOMISS/COMISS) and the recomputed bound (MULSS/ADDSS) are SINGLE precision and are modelled in float. The distance block (0x00fab061..0x00fab09a) is x87 from the first FLD onward: the three squares, their sum, the square root, the subtraction and the final FCOMIP all work at x87's 64-bit mantissa with nothing rounded to single precision in between, and it is modelled in long double for that reason. Rounding that block to float would not be this body.
mechanics.not_modelled: the x87 stack contents across a call (the model assumes the empty tag word MSVC's code assumes), and the identity of everything the six row objects, the three cleared .data words, 0x016c9e8c and 0x03fbae24 designate. The ECX receiver of 0x00fbf570 is passed as a declared sentinel rather than invented -- see mechanics.ecx_not_reloaded.
mechanics.ecx_not_reloaded: 0x00faaf0b is the only call in the body whose ECX the listing does not reload: the last write to ECX before it is MOV ECX,ESI at 0x00faaec4, eleven instructions earlier, for the slot+0x10 call, whose own return type this listing does not fix either. So the receiver of 0x00fbf570 is NOT DETERMINED by this body. The model passes the header's indeterminate_receiver() sentinel and the model test asserts the callee observer receives exactly that value, which makes the non-claim checkable rather than merely stated.
mechanics.globals: the complete 242-instruction listing names seven data-segment addresses and the body touches all seven: three .data words ZEROED (0x016c9e7c, 0x016c9e80, 0x016c9e84, a contiguous 12-byte run, at 0x00faaec8/0x00faaece/0x00faaed4, after the slot+0x10 call and before the counter increment), one .data ADDRESS PASSED BY VALUE with no read through it (0x016c9e8c, at 0x00faae86 -- Ghidra's decompilation of this VA prints it as &DAT_016c9e8c and the instruction bytes 68 8c 9e 6c 01 agree, so the two are the same value and the decompiler is right here), and three .rodata FLOATS read (0x01473c70 = 10.0f, 0x01485720 = 1.0f, 0x013ec4d0 = 100.0f, all read out of the image at their file offsets). The model keeps the three zeroed words in file-scope storage and re-poisons them between cases, because the interesting fact is their ORDER relative to the slot+0x10 call, not their value.

unresolved_questions: The committed ABI record's return_semantics is the phrase 'float_or_x87_in_ST0' and this package declares void. The record's own inference RT1 is an APPROXIMATION derived from a single observation -- 'an x87 or SSE instruction appears in the body' -- and the listing refutes it: the x87 stack is empty at 0x00faade0 and at 0x00fab0d1, because every x87 value the body produces is stored straight back or popped. The honest options were to declare a type true of the listing and record the disagreement (what this package does) or to declare void only if the bytes genuinely produce nothing (also true here, and the reason the choice is not a stretch). No typedef was invented to make the phrase compare equal, and the phrase itself is left intact in the evidence pack. The integrator should treat the record's return clause as superseded by the bytes.

What the three .data words at 0x016c9e7c, 0x016c9e80 and 0x016c9e84 are is not established. This body zeroes them and nothing else in the 242 instructions touches them, and no record in this repository names them. The address 0x016c9e8c, passed by value sixteen bytes higher and never read through, is plausibly part of the same structure, but nothing here establishes that and nothing is claimed.

What the literal 0x03fbae24 selects is not established. It is a 32-bit value, not a pointer (it is below the image's data segment) and not a float (as a float it would be about 1.09e-38, i.e. a denormal, which no compiler emits for a constant). Ghidra's own decompilation casts it to a pointer, which is the same 32 bits. This package carries it as an opaque Word named kStageId and claims nothing about it.

What the six objects at the receiver's +0x118 hold is not established. This body only LOADS each of the six words and passes it as a receiver to three callees; it never dereferences one. Whether they are sub-objects of this receiver, elements of an array, or something else is not determinable from this body, and the model deliberately names nothing inside them.

What the +0x111 byte is for is not established. It is the third disjunct of the resync condition, so setting it forces the resync block, and no instruction in this body writes it. Whether a sibling body writes it, and what setting it means, is outside what this listing can show.

What the relay word at the receiver's +0x81c holds is not established. This body clears it, hands the old value to 0x00690120, hands its ADDRESS to 0x00faacd0, and hands whatever 0x00faacd0 left to 0x006909b0 -- including a NULL receiver when the word started null. Whether that is a smart handle, a refcounted pointer or a plain word is not determinable here.

The ECX receiver of 0x00fbf570 is NOT DETERMINED by this body, and this package does not guess it. 0x00faaf0b is the only call whose ECX the listing does not reload; the last write is MOV ECX,ESI at 0x00faaec4 for the slot+0x10 call, whose return type this listing does not fix either. The model passes a declared sentinel and the model test asserts the callee receives exactly it, so the non-claim is checkable. Settling it needs 0x00fbf570's own body.

The conventions of six callees are asserted only as far as the call sites fix them. 0x0067dd80, 0x00690120, 0x006909b0, 0x00f96370, 0x00f96f90 and 0x00f977c0 are all called with no pushed word, so only 'receiver in ECX, no stack argument' is claimed; for a function with no stack arguments cdecl and thiscall are indistinguishable at the call site, and this package does not read the other five terminators to say more. 0x0067dd80's six bytes were read and it is a plain C3.

Nothing inside any of the fifteen direct callees was reconstructed, and no claim is made about any of them beyond the argument list, order and convention its call site fixes, plus the two callees whose own bodies were read out of the image (0x0067dd80 and 0x00f96370) because the body depends on what they do.

expected_reasons.GLOBALS: WARN, and it is an evidence ceiling rather than a defect. The complete 242-instruction listing names seven data-segment addresses (0x13ec4d0, 0x1473c70, 0x1485720, 0x16c9e7c, 0x16c9e80, 0x16c9e84, 0x16c9e8c) and the xref export carries no data-reference edge type at all, so there is no second machine side to corroborate read/write mode against. The source span deliberately names NONE of them: the three float constants are named constexprs, the three cleared words are file-scope model storage rather than a fixed address, and the 0x016c9e8c operand is a named Word. That is an honest PASS-shaped choice, not a dodge -- the body genuinely touches all seven, mechanics.globals lists each with its role and its instruction, and dropping the stores to win the check would have been a falsification of the body.

The naive literal scan would have attributed 0x34, 0x38, 0x3c, 0x369 and 0x374 to the receiver and reported a contradiction against the record; the alias-aware reading is the correct one and the check takes it.
